newsitem.title: POLAND: Decision on Prochnik stake sale postponed.
newsitem.headline: Decision on Prochnik stake sale postponed.

text.p: A court will decide on January 24 on whether a 25-percent stake of garment maker Prochnik, held by the receiver of its now-defunct shareholder insurer Westa, can be sold to a National Investment Fund, Westa's receiver said.
"The decision will be taken in seven days," Dorota Brzezinska-Grabarczyk told Reuters after Friday's court meeting, which was expected to settle the issue.

National Investment Fund No. 12, Piast, one of 15 such institutions created under the mass privatisation scheme, has offered to buy the Prochnik stake for 11 zlotys per share, more than the 9.19 zloty set by the receiver as the minimum price.

But the Securities Commission has said the deal would violate the law because the fund has not announced a public tender offer to buy the remaining Prochnik shares from other shareholders as required under the securities trading rules.
The Commission also said the fund ought to have notified it about the planned purchase.
